Thanks for reporting this!
I'll try to take a look. Have to admit that the styled-components wrapper is kind of an (cool) experiment, but styled-components it's not really built to be extensible. Pretty sure this is something we can fix on the react-pdf side though.
Btw, you can use the REPL as sandbox, including styled-components. Take a look [here](https://react-pdf.org/repl?)
Thanks for looking. I was trying to style a table and looking for a way to minimise duplicate style declarations by having the css for a cell (for example) being able to inherit the general cell styles and also specific column styles. The createStylesheet approach doesn't seem to support inheriting or extending styles whereas the styled component apparently does.

In the end I mostly worked around it by having components inheriting other components rather than styles so it's not urgent for me. However I guess if the styled components approach supports the syntax but not the functionality perhaps at least a warning should be emitted to make it clear and save anyone else spending time trying to figure out what they might be doing wrong. Hopefully it won't be the hardest thing to fix anyway since all the styles seems to be in there but just in a slightly broken format.

Also, thanks for the library. It's been very useful so far and hopefully can only get even better!
